Definition: A Chirality TASK skill that extracts typed dependency register edges from deliverable source documents.
A deliverable-local register made of Dependencies.csv v3.1 and _DEPENDENCIES.md.
The canonical structured dependency register output using v3.1 and 29 required columns.
The human-readable dependency index with declared lists, summary, run notes, run history, and lifecycle summary.
The required selector for deliverables, packages, or all deliverables under a run root.
Path to the run workspace.
Explicit path to the latest decomposition markdown.
AUTO or explicit list of filenames or paths to scan per deliverable.
Mapping of document roles to filename patterns for ANCHOR_DOC and EXECUTION_DOCS.
Primary anchor document controlling Pass 1 vertical Tree anchoring.
Ordered execution document list controlling Pass 2 horizontal DAG execution-edge extraction.
Update versus reset behavior for the run.
Extraction posture, either CONSERVATIVE or AGGRESSIVE.
Downstream consumer hint selector: NONE, TASK_ESTIMATING, AGGREGATION, or RECONCILIATION.
Deliverable-local read-only input used to resolve document pointers and TargetLocation.
Integrity preserved by two-pass extraction: Tree anchors before DAG execution edges.
Rows that connect a deliverable to an existing definition node and optionally requirement IDs.
Rows between deliverables or entities needed for prerequisites, handovers, constraints, or interfaces.
A dependency row classification whose write-form values are ANCHOR and EXECUTION.
DependencyClass value for rows connecting deliverables to definition nodes or requirement IDs.
DependencyClass value for rows capturing prerequisites, handovers, constraints, interfaces, and information transfer.
A row field whose write-form values are IMPLEMENTS_NODE, TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT, and NOT_APPLICABLE.
AnchorType for the single parent definition node.
AnchorType for requirement trace links.
AnchorType used by EXECUTION rows.
Field indicating dependency flow relative to this deliverable.
Direction meaning this deliverable requires information or assets from the target.
Direction meaning this deliverable produces information or assets for the target.
Execution dependency type with preferred values PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, and OTHER.
Target classification field with values such as DELIVERABLE, PACKAGE, WBS_NODE, REQUIREMENT, DOCUMENT, EQUIPMENT, EXTERNAL, and UNKNOWN.
Target classification used when a target cannot be resolved confidently.
Field populated with a local path when present, otherwise the best available pointer.
Evidence field identifying which source document supports a dependency row.
Evidence field identifying the source location supporting a dependency row.
Optional evidence excerpt limited to 30 words or fewer.
Extraction lifecycle field used with LastSeen and Status.
Extraction lifecycle field updated when found on later runs.
Extraction lifecycle field tracking whether a dependency relationship is currently observed.
Closure lifecycle field tracking whether the dependency has been fulfilled or remains open.
Closure lifecycle field tracked with ProposedMaturity and SatisfactionStatus.
Closure lifecycle field tracked with RequiredMaturity and SatisfactionStatus.
Optional extension column populated for TASK_ESTIMATING when evidence supports estimating relevance.
Optional extension column whose values classify estimating impact as BLOCKING, ADVISORY, INFO, or TBD.
_DEPENDENCIES.md section recording defaults, assumptions, paths, and warnings.
Append-only _DEPENDENCIES.md section with one entry per run.
_DEPENDENCIES.md section summarizing ACTIVE, RETIRED, and closure-state counts.
_DEPENDENCIES.md section added only when CONSUMER_CONTEXT is not NONE.
Dependency model purpose: dependencies capture information flow, artifact transfer, and explicit constraints.
